fips.counties

US county data

Examples

To get the county data for the WECC system use the command

from fips import Counties
print(Counties(use_index=["SYSTEM"],selection=["WECC"],set_index=["ST","COUNTY"]))

which outputs

              SYSTEM   FIPS        LAT  ...  DST    RO     REGION
ST COUNTY                               ...                      
AZ Apache       WECC   4001  35.385084  ...    1  WECC  SOUTHWEST
   Cochise      WECC   4003  31.840129  ...    0  WECC  SOUTHWEST
   Coconino     WECC   4005  35.829692  ...    1  WECC  SOUTHWEST
   Gila         WECC   4007  33.789618  ...    0  WECC  SOUTHWEST
   Graham       WECC   4009  32.931828  ...    0  WECC  SOUTHWEST
...              ...    ...        ...  ...  ...   ...        ...
WY Sweetwater   WECC  56037  41.660328  ...    1  WECC  NORTHWEST
   Teton        WECC  56039  44.048662  ...    1  WECC  NORTHWEST
   Uinta        WECC  56041  41.284726  ...    1  WECC  NORTHWEST
   Washakie     WECC  56043  43.878831  ...    1  WECC  NORTHWEST
   Weston       WECC  56045  43.846213  ...    1  WECC  NORTHWEST

Caveat

  • Some states have multiple regions. Only California and Nevada has county-level regions provided. All other states have the primary region specified, regardless of whether the state spans multiple regions.

  • Many counties are split among two or more regions.

   2
   3Examples
   4--------
   5

   8    from fips import Counties
   9    print(Counties(use_index=["SYSTEM"],selection=["WECC"],set_index=["ST","COUNTY"]))
  10
  11
  12which outputs
  13

  15    ST COUNTY                               ...                      
  16    AZ Apache       WECC   4001  35.385084  ...    1  WECC  SOUTHWEST
  17       Cochise      WECC   4003  31.840129  ...    0  WECC  SOUTHWEST

  19       Gila         WECC   4007  33.789618  ...    0  WECC  SOUTHWEST
  20       Graham       WECC   4009  32.931828  ...    0  WECC  SOUTHWEST
  21    ...              ...    ...        ...  ...  ...   ...        ...
  22    WY Sweetwater   WECC  56037  41.660328  ...    1  WECC  NORTHWEST
  23       Teton        WECC  56039  44.048662  ...    1  WECC  NORTHWEST
  24       Uinta        WECC  56041  41.284726  ...    1  WECC  NORTHWEST
  25       Washakie     WECC  56043  43.878831  ...    1  WECC  NORTHWEST

  27

  39from io import StringIO
  40
  41import pandas as pd
  42
  43REGIONS = {
  44    "ALASKA": "Alaska",
  45    "CAISO": "California Independent System Operator",
  46    "ERCOT": "Electric Reliability Council of Texas",
  47    "HAWAII": "Hawaii",
  48    "IID": "Imperial Irrigation District",
  49    "ISO-NE": "ISO New England",
  50    "LADWP": "Los Angeles Department of Water and Power",
  51    "MISO": "Midcontinent Independent System Operator",
  52    "NORTHWEST": "Northwest",
  53    "NYISO": "New York Independent System Operator",
  54    "PJM": "PJM Interconnection",
  55    "SOUTHEAST": "Southeast",
  56    "SOUTHWEST": "Southwest",
  57    "SPP": "Southwest Power Pool",
  58}
  59"""Valid `REGION` names and their descriptions"""
  60
  61class County:
  62    """Get county data
  63
  64    See `Counties()` for list of available county data. 
  65    """
  66    def __init__(self,**kwargs):
  67        """Construct a single county data object
  68
  69        # Arguments 
  70
  71        -  `**kwargs`: search criteria (e.g., `{ST="CA",COUNTY="Alameda"}`)
  72        """
  73        keys = list(kwargs.keys())
  74        values = list(kwargs.values())
  75
  76        try:
  77            self.data = Counties().set_index(keys).loc[[values]].reset_index()
  78        except KeyError:
  79            self.data = None
  80        if self.data is None or len(self.data) > 1:
  81            raise KeyError(f"{kwargs=} is not a valid unique key")
  82
  83    def __getattr__(self,key):
  84        return self.data[key].iloc[0]
  85
  86    def __str__(self):
  87        return f"{self.COUNTY} {self.ST} ({self.GEOHASH})"
  88
  89    def __repr__(self):
  90        return f"<County(FIPS={self.FIPS})>"
  91
  92    def to_dict(self):
  93        """Convert county data object to dict"""
  94        return {x:y[0] for x,y in self.data.to_dict('list').items()}
  95
  96class Counties(pd.DataFrame):
  97    """US counties dataframe
  98
  99    Columns
 100    -------
 101
 102      - `ST`: state abbreviation
 103
 104      - `FIPS`: county FIPS code
 105
 106      - `COUNTY`: county/parish/burrough name
 107    
 108      - `LAT`: county centroid latitude
 109
 110      - `LON`: county centroid longitude
 111
 112      - `GEOHASH`: county centroid geohash
 113
 114      - `TZOFFSET`: state timezone offset
 115
 116      - `DST`: flag to indicate whether summer time is observed
 117
 118      - `SYSTEM`: system interconnection name
 119
 120      - `RO`: reliability organization name
 121
 122      - `REGION`: electricity market or balancing region name (see `REGIONS`)
 123
 124    Caveat
 125    ------
 126
 127      - Some counties located along timezone boundaries may be split across
 128        two timezones. In such cases, the timezone selected covers the
 129        majority of the county's land area.
 130    """
 131    def __init__(self,
 132        state:str=None,
 133        use_index:str|list[str]=None,
 134        selection:list=None,
 135        set_index:str|list[str]=None
 136        ):
 137        """Construct a data frame of US counties
 138
 139        Arguments
 140        ---------
 141
 142          - `state`: state abbreviation
 143
 144          - `use_index`: use the specified column(s) as the index
 145
 146          - `selection`: row selection based on `use_index` 
 147
 148          - `set_index`: index to to set on data frame after row selection
 149        """
 150
 151        # See https://greenwichmeantime.com/time-zone/usa/{state}/counties/ for county timezones

62class County:
63    """Get county data
64
65    See `Counties()` for list of available county data. 
66    """
67    def __init__(self,**kwargs):
68        """Construct a single county data object
69
70        # Arguments 
71
72        -  `**kwargs`: search criteria (e.g., `{ST="CA",COUNTY="Alameda"}`)
73        """
74        keys = list(kwargs.keys())
75        values = list(kwargs.values())
76
77        try:
78            self.data = Counties().set_index(keys).loc[[values]].reset_index()
79        except KeyError:
80            self.data = None
81        if self.data is None or len(self.data) > 1:
82            raise KeyError(f"{kwargs=} is not a valid unique key")
83
84    def __getattr__(self,key):
85        return self.data[key].iloc[0]
86
87    def __str__(self):
88        return f"{self.COUNTY} {self.ST} ({self.GEOHASH})"
89
90    def __repr__(self):
91        return f"<County(FIPS={self.FIPS})>"
92
93    def to_dict(self):
94        """Convert county data object to dict"""
95        return {x:y[0] for x,y in self.data.to_dict('list').items()}

class Counties(pandas.DataFrame): 
  97class Counties(pd.DataFrame):
  98    """US counties dataframe
  99
 100    Columns
 101    -------
 102
 103      - `ST`: state abbreviation
 104
 105      - `FIPS`: county FIPS code
 106
 107      - `COUNTY`: county/parish/burrough name
 108    
 109      - `LAT`: county centroid latitude
 110
 111      - `LON`: county centroid longitude
 112
 113      - `GEOHASH`: county centroid geohash
 114
 115      - `TZOFFSET`: state timezone offset
 116
 117      - `DST`: flag to indicate whether summer time is observed
 118
 119      - `SYSTEM`: system interconnection name
 120
 121      - `RO`: reliability organization name
 122
 123      - `REGION`: electricity market or balancing region name (see `REGIONS`)
 124
 125    Caveat
 126    ------
 127
 128      - Some counties located along timezone boundaries may be split across
 129        two timezones. In such cases, the timezone selected covers the
 130        majority of the county's land area.
 131    """
 132    def __init__(self,
 133        state:str=None,
 134        use_index:str|list[str]=None,
 135        selection:list=None,
 136        set_index:str|list[str]=None
 137        ):
 138        """Construct a data frame of US counties
 139
 140        Arguments
 141        ---------
 142
 143          - `state`: state abbreviation
 144
 145          - `use_index`: use the specified column(s) as the index
 146
 147          - `selection`: row selection based on `use_index` 
 148
 149          - `set_index`: index to to set on data frame after row selection
 150        """
 151
 152        # See https://greenwichmeantime.com/time-zone/usa/{state}/counties/ for county timezones

US counties dataframe

Columns

  • ST: state abbreviation

  • FIPS: county FIPS code

  • COUNTY: county/parish/burrough name

  • LAT: county centroid latitude

  • LON: county centroid longitude

  • GEOHASH: county centroid geohash

  • TZOFFSET: state timezone offset

  • DST: flag to indicate whether summer time is observed

  • SYSTEM: system interconnection name

  • RO: reliability organization name

  • REGION: electricity market or balancing region name (see REGIONS)

Caveat

  • Some counties located along timezone boundaries may be split across two timezones. In such cases, the timezone selected covers the majority of the county's land area.
